title: Disambiguating Reference in Visually Grounded Dialogues through Joint Modeling of Textual and Multimodal Semantic Structures
research_question: Does jointly modeling textual reference relations such as coreference and predicate-argument structure with multimodal mention-to-object grounding improve the resolution of ambiguous and indirect references in visually grounded dialogue?
methodology: The approach jointly trains textual reference resolution and multimodal reference resolution components that share a text encoder while computing relation-specific similarities between textual mentions and between mentions and detected visual objects. Multimodal grounding uses a frozen Detic detector plus a trainable textual and cross-attention representation, while textual relations include coreference and predicate-argument relations that can supply additional semantic structure for ambiguous mentions. The authors evaluate phrase grounding and multimodal reference resolution on J-CRe3 and Flickr30k-Ent-JP, with additional Japanese textual-reference data used for the textual component. Recall@1, Recall@5, and Recall@10 are reported with an IoU threshold of 0.5, and experiments are repeated with three random seeds.

key_findings.finding: Adding the proposed textual-reference model substantially improved grounding of pronouns in J-CRe3: the coreference-enhanced model achieved Recall@1/5/10 of 0.361/0.683/0.772 versus 0.277/0.527/0.641 for the baseline.

For pronoun grounding, the coreference-enhanced model outperformed both GLIP and MDETR in the reported J-CRe3 comparison, even though GLIP remained stronger on overall phrase grounding at lower recall cutoffs.

Ablation experiments show that introducing textual reference relations improves pronoun grounding, with coreference providing the strongest individual benefit and combining relation types helping noun grounding.

The proposed multimodal-reference model consistently improves Recall@10 over the model without the added textual-reference information and can represent zero-reference cases that the GLIP-plus-parser comparison cannot directly handle.
Textual reference structure increases model confidence for relationships linking mentions, pronouns, predicates, and visually grounded objects in the qualitative analyses.

The results do not establish comparable behavior for non-Japanese dialogue, conversations with more than two participants, or grounding that requires consistent object identity across multiple images or document versions.

limitations: The experiments are limited primarily to Japanese-language data and do not establish multilingual generalization.
The visually grounded dialogue setting contains two-party interactions, so more complex participant structures remain untested.
Some indirect nominative and dative references in J-CRe3 tend to resolve to the master or robot, creating dataset-specific regularities.
The frozen Detic object detector can constrain noun grounding and contributes to weaker noun performance than stronger detection-grounding systems in some comparisons.
Grounding is performed from a single image at a time, making object consistency across changing visual contexts difficult.
The relationship between textual-reference-resolution quality and multimodal-reference-resolution quality requires more repeated and controlled analysis.
The study addresses conversational reference ambiguity but not longitudinal attachment revision, cross-version visual-region identity, or spreadsheet-specific references.
raw_claims: The model treats textual reference resolution and multimodal reference resolution as related tasks rather than independent problems.
The textual and multimodal components share a textual encoder.
Coreference, predicate-argument relations, and other textual links provide signals for disambiguating visually grounded mentions.
J-CRe3 contains visually grounded Japanese dialogue collected from interactions between a human master and an assistive robot.
The proposed textual-reference component provides especially large gains for pronoun grounding.
GLIP remains stronger on some overall phrase-grounding measures even though the proposed method is stronger for pronouns.
Different textual relation types make different contributions to noun and pronoun grounding.
The multimodal model can model references in which a predicate has no corresponding visual object.
Object detection is frozen during the multimodal-reference experiments.
The approach reasons from individual images and does not solve persistent object identity across multiple visual contexts.
The implementation and relevant datasets are publicly linked by the paper.
